metadata.case_name: CHIU TAK SANG v. KWAN HON LAM

injuries.description: the injury suffered by the Plaintiff was a compound dislocation of the right subtalar joint, which is located between the heel bone and the shin bone.
source: the injury suffered by the Plaintiff was a compound dislocation of the right subtalar joint, which is located between the heel bone and the shin bone.

injuries.description: X-ray examination in October this year showed that the Plaintiff has developed quite advanced post traumatic osteo-arthritis. The joint cartilage has been badly worn to the extent that it is now almost bone rubbing on bone.
source: X-ray examination in October this year showed that the Plaintiff has developed quite advanced post traumatic osteo-arthritis. The joint cartilage has been badly worn to the extent that it is now almost bone rubbing on bone.

manifestations.description: pain when walking or lifting heavy objects
now incapable of doing strenuous labouring work (cannot return to his work before the accident as a lorry attendant)
the condition will get continually worse
fusion operation will free him of pain but with the sacrifice of mobility

treatments_future: fusion operation of the subtalar joint (expected within 5 years)

losses.description: Pain when walking or lifting heavy objects resulting from advanced post traumatic osteo-arthritis of the right subtalar joint.
Sacrifice of mobility as a consequence of a future fusion operation that will be required to relieve pain.
Incapable of doing strenuous labouring work and cannot return to his work before the accident as a lorry attendant.

comparable_cases.injury_description: defined 'serious' category as 'a disability which mars general activities and enjoyment of life but allows reasonable mobility to the victim for example ... bad fractures leaving recurrent pain'.
Cheung J. in Chan Pui Ki revised the Lee Ting Man awards and gave a range for the 'serious' category from $400,000 to $540,000.
